raw_response:
I grow only cotton on my 20 mu, same as before. I do not like making big changes. What worked on nearby fields, I watch that, and then I do about the same or a little more if I can afford it. Cotton cannot be hungry early, or the plants stay weak, so I will put enough base fertilizer before sowing. On my land, with well water, I can push a bit more than dry land because if it turns dry, I can still give water. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose bolls later. For seed, I will use improved seed, because these years most people around here use better seed and it stands more even than the old saved kind. For tillage, I will plough first, because cotton likes loose soil and the roots go down better. Fertilizer, I will not do it light: I will figure around 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu for the year. Water, I will plan 4 times if the year is normal: once after seedlings settle, once before flowering, once at full flowering and boll setting, and once later if the soil turns dry. Pesticide, I will not wait for trouble to get bad; on 20 mu I cannot afford a heavy pest year, so I will plan about 5 sprays through the season for aphids, bollworm, and mites if they show up. If the weather is good and I manage on time, I will count on about 350 kg per mu. That is what I will aim for this year.
